quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when stopping takes longer than usual, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy. Rain makes it harder to stop quickly.

questions.question: How do you shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push down.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
questions.explanation: To shift up to a higher gear, position your foot under the shift lever and lift it upward.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs more frequent attention than a car. You must check your motorcycle regularly. If something is wrong, find it before riding in traffic or on highways.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, how should motorcyclists ride?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close together while giving each rider enough space. Switch to single-file when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving the road.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay within the posted speed limits.
Go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: Always complete passes within the legal speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell you about traffic laws in that area. This sign says right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What should you wear to be more visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding. Other drivers will see you more easily, no matter what time of day it is.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving over bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get across faster.
Keep the same speed and ride straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the same speed and ride straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle starts to weave on bridge gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight. Zigzagging to stay in your lane is dangerous.

questions.question: Which factor affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: The main factors that affect BAC are how much alcohol someone drank, how fast they drank it, and their body weight.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if there is other traffic.
Vehicles will enter the road soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop. Let all crossing traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What can cause motorcycle collisions?

options.text: Following too closely behind another vehicle
Honking the horn at the wrong time

questions.correctAnswerText: Following too closely behind another vehicle
questions.explanation: Following too closely, called "tailgating," causes many motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What is the legal blood alcohol content (BAC) limit for operating a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: In California, drivers age 21 or older cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Drivers under 21 cannot operate with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Even below the legal limit, alcohol can make riding unsafe.

questions.question: What can happen if you lock your brakes?
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes causes control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and then apply it again. If your rear brake locks on a surface with good traction, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT greatly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: The main factors that affect BAC are how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required equipment on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, motorcycles must have: a seat for the operator; seats and footrests for passengers; a muffler; a rear reflector; a rearview mirror; a horn; brakes; headlights; a white license plate light; and a red stop light. A yellow stop light is not required.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel locks while stopping?

options.text: Release the front brake and only use the rear brake
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again firmly

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again firmly
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks during a quick stop, release the front brake immediately and then apply it firmly again. Use both the front and rear brakes together when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: How many drinks affect your ability to ride safely?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can hurt your ability to ride safely. Never ride a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to hazards
You have more time to speed up when entering a curve

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to speed up when entering a curve
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if another driver makes a mistake. Extra space does not help you accelerate into curves.

questions.question: What should you do before riding a borrowed motorcycle?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same place as your motorcycle
Take it directly onto the highway
Learn how to use it in a safe, controlled area first

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn how to use it in a safe, controlled area first
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle on the road, learn where all the controls are. Practice riding it in a controlled area until you are comfortable with it.

questions.question: Keeping space around your motorcycle allows you to do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely if another driver makes a mistake. Space is for safety, not for showing off.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger on your motorcycle, what should you tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the rider.

questions.question: Why is stopping in a turn difficult on a motorcycle?

options.text: There is less grip available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
The rider is usually focused on the turn and not on braking.
The brakes do not work in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less grip available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle leans to turn, some grip is used for the turn. This means less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: Which surface is potentially slippery?
questions.explanation: Poor grip can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement. Gravel roads, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers are also slippery.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It is white with red and black markings. It tells drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What type of gloves should you wear when riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Wear full-fingered gloves made of strong material.
